This is a typical AUR package for Qt/Python bindings with no supply-chain attack indicators in the global scope.

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD follows standard Arch Linux packaging practices: it declares a single source tarball fetched from the project’s own GitHub repository using a normal AUR source line, includes a checksum, and runs conventional build steps (`cmake`, `python setup.py`). All post‑install and package‑specific functions use `cmake --install` and safe helper functions to copy Python egg‑info and create a lightweight wrapper for the Qt6 designer. No external network calls, code execution, obfuscation, or dangerous commands (`eval`, `curl`, `wget`, base64) appear in the file. The only custom script (`pyside6-designer`) merely sets `LD_PRELOAD` and execs `designer6`, a benign packaging convenience.

Overall, there is no evidence of malicious activity, data exfiltration, or injected code. The build process is reproducible and transparent, adhering to typical AUR conventions.
</details>
